  id = {EDN-73},
  title = {Hyperparameters change only under a written tuning protocol},
  note = {\textbf{Absorbs EDN-70 and EDN-78} (2026-10-05, 2026-10-06): the tree ceiling, and the search over both LightGBM variants.},
  date = {2026-10-05},
  milestone = {M3: Quality Assurance},
  topic = {Hyperparameter Tuning, Evaluation Protocol},
  participants = {@lukas2510; @kadameit decided the search over both variants (2026-10-06)},
  decision = {\texttt{learning\_\allowbreak{}rate} 0.05 and \texttt{num\_\allowbreak{}leaves} 63 stay, because no search found a point that the validation split can tell apart from them.
A committed hyperparameter is replaced only under the protocol in the pipeline docs: selection on the validation split alone, by validation L1, and only when the simultaneous 95\,\% interval of the difference lies below zero.
\texttt{n\_\allowbreak{}estimators} is a ceiling of 5,000 with early stopping after 50 rounds.
\texttt{tune.\allowbreak{}py} runs a search outside \texttt{dvc repro}; its record lives in MLflow only, and its energy is reported apart from NFR-10's budget.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item Adopt the point with the lowest validation L1: its gain lies inside the noise.
\item Random or Optuna search with cross-validation: a new dependency and about five times the fits, for a region found flat.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} Across the twelve points of the first grid, no interval of the difference to the committed point lies below zero.
With the higher ceiling, the validation curve decides how many trees a model keeps.
The search of 2026-10-06 covered both LightGBM variants and \texttt{min\_\allowbreak{}child\_\allowbreak{}samples}, reproduced the first grid, and kept the committed values in all four sweeps.},
  ai = {Information seeking, Alternative generation, Alternative assessment, Recommendation, Solution generation},
  response = {Accepted with modifications},
  assessment = {AI designed the first sweep and stopped for the decision instead of committing a tuned value.
An independent AI review corrected the protocol: its first rule used an interval per point, which is not safe across eleven comparisons.
For the search of 2026-10-06 AI recommended committing the sweep records beside MLflow; Kevin had it check the course demo, which keeps its emissions in MLflow only, and chose that.},
  aievidence = {Claude Code sessions of 2026-10-05 (issue \#64) and of 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-09 (issue \#88).},
